fullPassage: Covering the president has become an industry unto itself. Hundreds of "beat reporters" - journalists who cover the White House on a daily basis - work from the basement of the White House. Twice a day, these reporters meet with the president's press secretary to get a briefing on the day's activities. Television cameras covering these briefings have been a frequent source of conflict between the press secretary and the press, as some journalists use these press briefings as an opportunity to grandstand for the cameras. Typically, the press is on call twenty-four hours a day, unless the press secretary puts a "lid" on the news, which means that no big announcements are planned. Most presidents have "feuded" with particular journalists and publications at one time or another. Richard Nixon disliked the Washington Post and New York Times, and had his vice president publicly attack them. The Clinton White House singled out Sue Schmidt of the Washington Post as a reporter with a vendetta against the president. President George W. Bush publicly used a rude word to describe New York Times reporter Adam Clymer, a sentiment that Vice President Cheney agreed with. President Kennedy, on the other hand, enjoyed a friendly relationship with the press corps, partly because he singled out favorites for special treatment in return for favorable coverage. In spite of the tension between the president and the press corps, the two have a symbiotic relationship. The president needs the press to deliver his message, and the press needs access to the president in order to do its job. It's not uncommon for White House staffers to leak information to select journalists in order to shape the coverage. Sometimes the president will grant exclusive interviews to certain reporters as a way to dominate the headlines.

F — 본문에 명시되어 있으므로 불일치가 아님
det.tip: Twice a day(하루 두 번) + meet ... to get a briefing(브리핑을 받는다) = 일치

questions.passage: Covering the president has become an industry unto itself. Hundreds of "beat reporters" - journalists who cover the White House on a daily basis - work from the basement of the White House. Twice a day, these reporters meet with the president's press secretary to get a briefing on the day's activities. Television cameras covering these briefings have been a frequent source of conflict between the press secretary and the press, as some journalists use these press briefings as an opportunity to grandstand for the cameras. Typically, the press is on call twenty-four hours a day, unless the press secretary puts a "lid" on the news, which means that no big announcements are planned. Most presidents have "feuded" with particular journalists and publications at one time or another. Richard Nixon disliked the Washington Post and New York Times, and had his vice president publicly attack them. The Clinton White House singled out Sue Schmidt of the Washington Post as a reporter with a vendetta against the president. President George W. Bush publicly used a rude word to describe New York Times reporter Adam Clymer, a sentiment that Vice President Cheney agreed with. President Kennedy, on the other hand, enjoyed a friendly relationship with the press corps, partly because he singled out favorites for special treatment in return for favorable coverage. In spite of the tension between the president and the press corps, the two have a symbiotic relationship. The president needs the press to deliver his message, and the press needs access to the president in order to do its job. It's not uncommon for White House staffers to leak information to select journalists in order to shape the coverage. Sometimes the president will grant exclusive interviews to certain reporters as a way to dominate the headlines.
questions.stem:
글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"조지 W. 부시 대통령이 애덤 클라이머를 묘사한 표현에 체니 부통령은 반대했다."

det.korean: a sentiment that Vice President Cheney agreed with. 체니 부통령은 부시의 표현에 '동의했다(agreed)'고 했으므로 '반대했다'는 불일치이다.
det.analysis:
T — 체니가 부시와 의견이 달랐다는 것은 본문과 반대

F — a sentiment that Vice President Cheney agreed with, 체니가 동의했다고 했으므로 '반대했다'는 사실이 아님 ←정답
det.tip: Cheney agreed with Bush's sentiment = 동의했음(반대했다는 불일치)

det.korean: 글은 대통령과 언론 사이에 반목(feud)도 있지만 서로 필요로 하는 공생 관계(symbiotic relationship)도 있다는 점을 다룬다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 하루 일정 — 초반 몇 문장의 소재일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님

❌ ② 선호 신문사 목록 — 세부 사례일 뿐 주제가 아님

✅ ③ 대통령과 언론 사이의 갈등과 상호 의존이 공존하는 관계 — 반목 사례들 + the two have a symbiotic relationship, needs ~ needs를 종합 ←정답

❌ ④ 뉴스 발표 시점 조절 — 'lid' 언급은 일부 세부사항일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
